name: The Divided Monarchy
subtitle: Two kingdoms, one timeline
blurb: From the schism at Shechem to the fall of Jerusalem — every king of both kingdoms, the years Kings tells in a braid no reader can untangle from the prose alone.
howToRead: Time runs left to right; the two tracks are the two kingdoms. Each block is a reign, sized to its length and stamped at its left edge with the Deuteronomistic verdict — right, evil, or mixed (right, but the high places remained). Click a reign for its accession formula, the cross-kingdom synchronism the text itself states, and the chapters that carry it. The diamonds on the central spine are the events the reigns hang on.
seedNote: This edition runs the whole Divided Monarchy — all forty kings of both kingdoms, from the schism (931) to the fall of Samaria (722) and the fall of Jerusalem (586). Dates follow Thiele; where the text's regnal total counts a co-regency (Jeroboam II, Uzziah, Jotham, Manasseh) the block shows the sole reign and the note explains. The hardest stretch is Menahem–Pekah, where the synchronisms genuinely strain — Pekah's stated twenty years is the knot Thiele unties with a rival reign.

lanes.name: Israel — the North
lanes.note: Ten tribes · no Davidic king · every ruler "did evil"

lanes.name: Judah — the South
lanes.note: Davidic line unbroken · the temple · verdicts run mixed

spans.label: Jeroboam I
spans.note: Led the ten tribes out; set up golden calves at Dan and Bethel so the people would not go up to Jerusalem — "the sin of Jeroboam" that the book measures every northern king against.

spans.label: Nadab
spans.aside: Began to reign in the second year of Asa of Judah.
spans.note: Struck down by Baasha while besieging a Philistine town; the house of Jeroboam is wiped out, as the prophet Ahijah foretold.

spans.label: Baasha
spans.aside: Began to reign in the third year of Asa of Judah.
spans.note: Usurper who walked in the way of Jeroboam; warred with Asa over the border fortress of Ramah.

spans.label: Elah
spans.note: Killed by his chariot commander Zimri while drinking himself drunk in Tirzah.

spans.label: Zimri
spans.note: Reigned seven days. When the army proclaimed Omri instead, he burned the palace down over himself.

spans.label: Omri
spans.note: Won a four-year civil war against Tibni, bought the hill of Samaria and built his capital there. "Did worse than all who were before him" — yet Assyria called the north "the house of Omri" for a century after.

spans.label: Ahab
spans.aside: Began to reign in the thirty-eighth year of Asa of Judah.
spans.note: Married Jezebel of Sidon and made Baal worship state policy; the Elijah cycle is set against his reign. Died at Ramoth-Gilead by a bow drawn at random.

spans.label: Ahaziah
spans.note: Fell through a lattice and sent to Baal-zebub of Ekron rather than the LORD; Elijah meets the messengers with a word of death.

spans.label: Joram (Jehoram)
spans.aside: Began to reign in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat of Judah.
spans.note: Last of the Omrides. Wounded fighting Aram at Ramoth-Gilead; killed at Jezreel by Jehu, his body thrown on Naboth's field.

spans.label: Jehu
spans.note: Anointed by Elisha's man to cut off the house of Ahab; killed Joram, Ahaziah of Judah, Jezebel, and the priests of Baal. Yet he kept the golden calves — zeal against Baal, not against the sin of Jeroboam.

spans.label: Jehoahaz
spans.aside: Began to reign in the twenty-third year of Joash of Judah.
spans.note: Israel ground down to almost nothing under Hazael of Aram. Yet when Jehoahaz sought the LORD's favor, God gave Israel a deliverer — the one crack of mercy in the dynasty.

spans.label: Jehoash (Joash)
spans.aside: Began to reign in the thirty-seventh year of Joash of Judah.
spans.note: Wept over the dying Elisha — "my father, my father, the chariots of Israel" — and recovered three cities from Aram as the prophet foretold. Defeated Amaziah of Judah and broke down the wall of Jerusalem.

spans.label: Jeroboam II
spans.aside: Began to reign in the fifteenth year of Amaziah of Judah.
spans.note: The longest, richest northern reign (co-regent from c. 793). Restored Israel's borders from Lebo-hamath to the Dead Sea, as Jonah son of Amittai had spoken. It is this prosperity — and the injustice under it — that Amos and Hosea indict.

spans.label: Zechariah
spans.note: Reigned six months, then was struck down in public by Shallum — ending the house of Jehu in the fourth generation, exactly as the LORD had promised Jehu.

spans.label: Shallum
spans.note: One month in Samaria. Menahem came up from Tirzah and killed him — the north now devours its own kings in a season.

spans.label: Menahem
spans.note: Brutal even by the north's measure — sacked Tiphsah and ripped open its pregnant women. Bought off Pul (Tiglath-Pileser III) with a thousand talents of silver, taxing the wealthy. Assyria is now on the doorstep.

spans.label: Pekahiah
spans.note: Menahem's son. Killed in the palace citadel by his own captain Pekah and fifty Gileadites.

spans.label: Pekah
spans.note: The text gives him twenty years — a total Thiele reads as a rival reign running back into Menahem's. Joined Rezin of Aram against Judah; in answer Tiglath-Pileser stripped Galilee and Gilead and deported them. Hoshea conspired and killed him.

spans.label: Hoshea
spans.aside: Began to reign in the twelfth year of Ahaz of Judah.
spans.note: The last king of Israel — "yet not as the kings of Israel before him." Withheld tribute and intrigued with So of Egypt; Assyria besieged Samaria three years and carried the north away for good.

spans.label: Rehoboam
spans.note: Solomon's son. His harsh answer at Shechem splits the kingdom; Judah "did what was evil," building high places and pillars.

spans.label: Abijah (Abijam)
spans.aside: Began to reign in the eighteenth year of Jeroboam of Israel.
spans.note: Walked in his father's sins; yet "for David's sake" the LORD kept a lamp in Jerusalem.

spans.label: Asa
spans.aside: Began to reign in the twentieth year of Jeroboam of Israel.
spans.note: "Did what was right" — put away the idols, even deposed his mother for her Asherah — but the high places were not removed.

spans.label: Jehoshaphat
spans.aside: Began to reign in the fourth year of Ahab of Israel.
spans.note: Walked in the way of Asa; allied with Ahab by marriage — the alliance that would nearly cost Judah the Davidic line.

spans.label: Jehoram
spans.aside: Began to reign in the fifth year of Joram of Israel.
spans.note: Married a daughter of Ahab and "walked in the way of the kings of Israel"; killed his own brothers. Judah's verdict turns north.

spans.label: Ahaziah
spans.aside: Began to reign in the twelfth year of Joram of Israel.
spans.note: Grandson of both Jehoshaphat and Ahab. Visiting wounded Joram at Jezreel, he is caught in Jehu's purge and killed.

spans.label: Athaliah
spans.note: Ahab's daughter. Seeing her son dead, she destroys the royal seed and seizes the throne — the one break in the Davidic line, six years when the lamp nearly went out.

spans.label: Joash
spans.aside: Began to reign in the seventh year of Jehu of Israel.
spans.note: Hidden as an infant in the temple by his aunt, crowned at seven by the priest Jehoiada. Did right all the days of Jehoiada — and repaired the temple — but the high places remained.

spans.label: Amaziah
spans.aside: Began to reign in the second year of Jehoash of Israel.
spans.note: Did right, "yet not like David" — and the high places remained. Executed his father's assassins but spared their children, as the law commands. Beat Edom, then provoked Jehoash of Israel and was crushed; assassinated at Lachish.

spans.label: Azariah (Uzziah)
spans.aside: Began to reign in the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam of Israel.
spans.note: A long, strong reign (co-regent from c. 792). Struck with leprosy — Chronicles says for usurping the priest's office to burn incense — he lived in a separate house while his son Jotham governed. Isaiah's call comes "in the year that King Uzziah died."

spans.label: Jotham
spans.aside: Began to reign in the second year of Pekah of Israel.
spans.note: Governed through his father's leprosy and did right — but again the high places stood. In his days the LORD "began to send" Rezin and Pekah against Judah: the storm gathers.

spans.label: Ahaz
spans.aside: Began to reign in the seventeenth year of Pekah of Israel.
spans.note: Walked in the way of the kings of Israel — even burned his son as an offering. Cornered by Aram and Israel, he hired Tiglath-Pileser, stripped the temple to pay him, and copied a pagan altar. To this faithless king Isaiah gave the sign of Immanuel.

spans.label: Hezekiah
spans.aside: Began to reign in the third year of Hoshea of Israel.
spans.note: The rare unqualified verdict — he removed the high places, even broke up Moses' bronze serpent. "He trusted in the LORD; there was none like him." Survived Sennacherib's siege when the angel struck the Assyrian camp; Isaiah his prophet.

spans.label: Manasseh
spans.note: Longest reign of any king of Judah (co-regent from c. 697) and its darkest — rebuilt the high places, set an idol in the temple, "shed innocent blood very much." For Manasseh's sins, Kings says, Judah would finally be cast out. (Chronicles adds his captivity and repentance.)

spans.label: Amon
spans.note: Walked in all his father's idolatry without the repentance. Killed by his own servants in the palace; the people of the land avenged him and made Josiah king.

spans.label: Josiah
spans.note: The great reformer. When the Book of the Law was found in the temple he tore his clothes, purged the high places root and branch, kept a Passover unlike any since the judges. "Before him there was no king like him" who turned to the LORD with all his heart. Killed at Megiddo facing Pharaoh Neco.

spans.label: Jehoahaz
spans.note: Three months. Pharaoh Neco put him in chains at Riblah and carried him to Egypt, where he died — the first of Judah's kings to end in a foreign land.

spans.label: Jehoiakim
spans.note: Neco's appointee (Eliakim, renamed). Taxed the land to pay tribute, burned Jeremiah's scroll column by column. Became Nebuchadnezzar's vassal, then rebelled — and Babylon began to close in.

spans.label: Jehoiachin
spans.note: Three months, then surrender. Deported to Babylon with the officials, craftsmen, and the temple gold — the 597 exile, Ezekiel among the carried-off. Released from prison decades later: the book's last, faint flicker of hope.

spans.label: Zedekiah
spans.aside: Babylon's appointee (Mattaniah, renamed) — uncle of Jehoiachin.
spans.note: The last king. Rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar; when the city fell he watched his sons killed at Riblah, then was blinded and carried to Babylon. The Davidic throne goes dark.

events.label: The schism at Shechem
events.note: Rehoboam answers the elders' counsel with the young men's — "my father chastised you with whips, I with scorpions" — and the ten tribes break away under Jeroboam.

events.label: Shishak plunders the temple
events.note: In Rehoboam's fifth year, Pharaoh Sheshonq I takes the treasures of the house of the LORD; the gold shields are replaced with bronze.

events.label: Elijah on Carmel
events.note: The contest with the prophets of Baal during Ahab's reign — "the LORD, he is God." Date is set by the reign, not fixed in the text.

events.label: Battle of Qarqar
events.note: Shalmaneser III's inscription names "Ahab the Israelite" with 2,000 chariots in a coalition against Assyria. Not in Scripture — but the single firmest peg anchoring the biblical chronology to the Assyrian record, and so the keystone of Thiele's dates used here.

events.label: Jehu's revolt
events.note: The hinge of these years: in a single campaign Jehu kills Joram of Israel, Ahaziah of Judah, and Jezebel, ending the house of Omri in both kingdoms at once. Athaliah answers by seizing Judah's throne.

events.label: Amos and Hosea indict the North
events.note: At the height of Jeroboam II's prosperity, the two prophets name the rot beneath it — Israel's injustice, its unfaithfulness — a generation before Assyria comes to collect.

events.label: The Syro-Ephraimite war
events.note: Pekah of Israel and Rezin of Aram march on Jerusalem to force Judah into their coalition against Assyria. Ahaz buys Tiglath-Pileser III instead, who strips Galilee. To Ahaz, Isaiah gives the sign of Immanuel.

events.label: Fall of Samaria
events.note: Assyria takes Samaria and deports the north. The writer stops the narrative to deliver his verdict, in full, on why the kingdom of Israel ended: they feared other gods. The northern track ends here.

events.label: Sennacherib at the gates
events.note: Assyria takes the fortified cities of Judah and besieges Jerusalem. Hezekiah trusts, Isaiah prophesies, and the Assyrian camp is struck in the night — the deliverance Samaria, twenty years before, never had.

events.label: The Book of the Law is found
events.note: Repairing the temple, Hilkiah finds the book; Josiah tears his clothes and launches the deepest reform in Judah's history, tearing down the high places his fathers kept rebuilding.

events.label: Josiah falls at Megiddo
events.note: Josiah marches against Pharaoh Neco and is killed. With him dies the last good reign; within months Judah passes under Egyptian, then Babylonian, control.

events.label: The first deportation
events.note: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jerusalem, deports Jehoiachin with the officials and craftsmen, and empties the temple treasury — eleven years before the city itself burns.

events.label: Fall of Jerusalem
events.note: Babylon breaches the city, burns the temple, and carries Judah into exile — the far edge of the Kings narrative. Throne ended, temple ashes, the people carried off.
